description: viber hooks: injects the viber manifest at session start, and gates ExitPlanMode on a review of the plan. The SessionStart hook writes hooks/content/manifest.md verbatim into the main session's context once per session (source == "resume" excluded, since the prior injection reloads with the transcript) and falls back to the version banner alone when that file is empty or unreadable. The banner gains a schema note when the project's .claude/viber.yml schema lags the plugin template's (run /viber:setup) or is ahead of it (update the plugin), and stays plain when the numbers match or no file exists. The plan gate is armed only when the current plan-mode episode shows a Write/Edit of a plans/*.md file; the reviewer is viber:planner-review when the planner skill ran in the episode (a Skill tool_use, plugin prefix included) and the plan file opens with the planner frontmatter source: line (an unreadable plan keeps planner-review), otherwise viber:plain-plan-review, and only when .claude/viber.yml turns planning.plain-plan-review on. Anything else - planning.plain-plan-review off, an exit in a session that already built a plan - passes untouched. When armed it allows ExitPlanMode only after a dispatch of that reviewer that followed the last plan write returned 'VERDICT: PASS', with the plan file untouched since that verdict (mtime vs. the transcript timestamp). The UserPromptSubmit hook adds plan-writing hints (a closing subagent review task, parallel subagents for independent tasks) to every prompt sent in plain plan mode, silent once the planner, intent or fixer skill ran in the episode. The PreToolUse hook on Bash (kill-guard.sh) refuses, inside a viber agent (agent_type starting with viber:), a command that stops processes by name - killall, pkill, taskkill with /IM, xargs running kill, kill fed by a command substitution - and tells the agent to stop only the PIDs it started with kill <PID>; it is silent for the main session, other agents and every other command, and never answers allow. All four hooks fail open: any parse miss or unreadable input allows. The function-hook module monitor/register.tsx is the read-only build monitor: at session start it reads build.monitor through config.sh and stays silent unless it is true; otherwise it tracks viber:task-coder and viber:task-reviewer spawns and the end of their runs, refreshes the active run through plan-path.sh and plan-index.sh (never --split, every run with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0) at session start, at each such spawn and end, after a Bash call running commit-task.sh and on a clock while a build is observed, and pins the status line; it passes every event on unchanged and writes nothing.
